2026-09-16T18:07Z.note: Aggressive-mode dig (deliberate, after 4 quiet cycles): spot-checked all 3 flat_theta_bleed exits today (CORZ/ALAB/SMTC) against their own ledger peak/trough fields. Found CORZ exit_detail is factually wrong: claims "never left the +-10% band" but trough was -13.64% (entry 0.22, trough 0.19) -- outside the band. Traced root cause: ExitEngineInput has no troughPremium field at all, evaluateLedgerRowExit never reads row.trough_premium -- the flat-timeout condition is structurally blind to downside excursions, only checks peak+current. This is systemic (will recur on any play that dips below -10% then recovers), not a one-off. Two possible fixes with very different stakes: narrative-only (plumb trough through, soften the sentence) vs behavior-changing (trough breach disqualifies the flat scratch, changing which plays get exited). Only 1 confirmed instance today -- reported with full evidence on PR #4076, NOT fixed (ambiguous, touches live exit decisions, n=1 vs the 3-instance threshold). Board otherwise unchanged, same 9 closed positions.

open_findings.summary: src/features/nighthawk/command-deck/PlayTerminal.tsx:876 (ZeroDtePreEntryContext, the 0DTE pre-entry Risk:Reward line) has the IDENTICAL root-cause bug the Legacy lane just fixed and shipped in deterministic-edition.ts (PR #4813, merged sha ab3781aae): `{rr.toFixed(1)}:1{rr >= 2 ? " (strong)" : rr >= 1 ? " (favorable)" : rr >= 0.5 ? " (acceptable)" : " (tight)"}` rounds the DISPLAYED number to-nearest with toFixed(1) while the quality label buckets on the TRUE unrounded `rr` (play.rrRatio) against the exact same threshold ladder (2 / 1 / 0.5) the rounded display can cross. Any rr just under a threshold (e.g. 0.49, 0.95, 1.95) displays as exactly the threshold value ("0.5", "1.0", "2.0") while the label still reads the lower bucket -- e.g. "0.5:1 (tight)" where "tight" is defined as < 0.5, self-contradicting the printed number the same way the Legacy thesis text did before the fix.

reference_fix_already_shipped_elsewhere.fix_pattern: Replace `rr.toFixed(1)` with a floor-based display value so the shown number can never read at-or-above a threshold the true rr hasn't reached: `const rrDisplay = Math.floor(rr * 10 + 1e-9) / 10;` then display `rrDisplay.toFixed(1)`, keep the label bucketing on the TRUE unrounded rr exactly as-is. The 1e-9 epsilon guards a clean multiple of 0.1 (e.g. exactly 0.50) from floor()'ing down one tick due to binary floating-point representation.

open_findings.root_cause_hypothesis_not_db_confirmed: Traced two candidate layers, not fully confirmed without direct Postgres access (blocked in this sandbox): (1) src/lib/platform/zerodte-service.ts:494-499 `boardClosedReason` fallback is `engineExitCategory ?? "time_stop"` -- UNCONDITIONAL, not gated on whether nowEtMinutes is actually near/past PLAN_RULES.time_stop_et_minutes (15:50 ET). This is a real logic defect independent of any timing race: ANY row whose engineExitCategory cannot be derived (missing/stale entry_context.exit, unmapped reason) gets mislabeled "time_stop" specifically, regardless of actual time of day -- CMPS closed at ~12:02 ET, nowhere near the real time-stop threshold, yet got that exact label. (2) src/lib/zerodte/scan.ts syncLedgerLiveState (~line 2722-2728): the in-memory `nextRow` returned after an exit-engine EXIT is `{...r, status, last_mark, peak_premium, trough_premium}` -- it does NOT merge in the entry_context that evaluateLedgerRowExit just wrote to Postgres via stampZeroDteExitContext (exit-sync.ts:515-518, a separate best-effort DB write). So the SAME request/tick that closes a play via the exit engine would always render that build with a stale entry_context (no .exit) -- self-correcting only once a LATER buildZeroDteBoardPayload does a fresh readZeroDteLedgerChecked() DB read that picks up the by-then-persisted stamp. Does not fully explain why THIS instance took ~20 minutes across 3 distinct polls when the warm cron runs ~every 5 min -- that gap is the part still needing DB-side confirmation (e.g. whether readZeroDteLedgerChecked is itself served from a cache layer this sandbox cannot inspect, or whether some other condition kept re-selecting the stale row).

known_explained_patterns.pattern: commit_ready=1 in session_stats persisting for 30-90+ seconds (or briefly flickering back to BLOCKED) without the setup appearing in board.ledger or /record
known_explained_patterns.note: NOT a bug -- by design. session_stats.commit_ready is computed live per API read by tallySetupGateLanes() (session-board-stats.ts) against the CURRENT setups[] gate.verdict -- a fresh, continuously-recomputed snapshot. Actual execution into the ledger happens on the zerodte-warm cron (cron-registry.ts: schedule_label ~every 5 min market hours, in-app leader fills sub-5m gaps), which runs warmZeroDteBoard on its own cadence, independent of any single board read. So a setup can legitimately show commit_ready=1 for up to ~5 minutes (or briefly revert to BLOCKED on fresh quotes/VIX before the warm tick ever runs) without indicating a stuck or lost commit window. First observed as NVDA flicker at the 14:15Z cycle, then TEM sitting commit_ready 90s+ at 14:33Z -- traced same cycle. Would still flag if a specific setup sits commit_ready past ~2 warm-cron cycles (~10min) without ever committing or reverting to blocked -- that would be the actual anomalous shape.
